attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The context (slight liberal bias, bland opinions) shows he means expressed views. 'Thus far' is kept. This is a firm observation backed by an appeal to studies.

contract.note: The plain reading (same broad lean, narrow range, some difference in degree allowed) is how an ordinary reader would take 'not that different' in this context. No threshold was given, so judgment is still needed.

evidence.note: PLOS press release on a peer-reviewed study of 24 major LLMs, published July 2024: most were left-of-center on most tests. Inside the period.
Stanford GSB release on a May 2025 study of 24 LLMs from 8 firms: nearly all responses were seen as left-leaning on 18 of 30 questions. A second independent study, before the post date.
Firms differed in degree (OpenAI four times Google; Google and DeepSeek near neutral), but all ranged from neutral to left and none was clearly right. This limits the claim without reversing it.

reviews.rationale: Two comparative studies out by mid-2025 found that most major LLMs land in the same neutral-to-left area. That meets the support condition. The differences in degree in e3 do not amount to clearly different positions, so the contradiction condition is not met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post.

semantics.note: It captures both the universal incoherence claim and its stated cause (parroting inconsistent training data instead of reasoning).

contract.note: Asking for evidence on both the incoherence and its cause is fair for a 'because' claim. 'Fully coherent' and 'parrot vs reasoning' are hard to operationalise, so the result depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: ACL 2024 paper: model opinions shift with forcing and lack paraphrase robustness. This backs the incoherence part for the models tested but says nothing about the cause.
Rozado preprint: political preferences may be instilled mostly after pretraining. It is preliminary and about where the views come from, not about coherence, so it does not settle the causal part.

reviews.rationale: The incoherence part has partial support for the models tested, but no evaluation covers every LLM. No study in the packet tests whether conflicting training data causes the inconsistency, and e2 is not about coherence. The support condition for both parts is not met, and nothing clearly contradicts the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post.

semantics.note: The sentence answers his own question about why models cluster near the middle, so adding the causal link is faithful to the context. 'Heretofore' and 'pretty much every' are kept.

contract.note: The two-part test (shared web data, and shared data as the cause of clustering) follows his words. 'More or less the same' has no overlap threshold, and frontier training data is undisclosed.

evidence.note: Mozilla: at least 64% of 47 LLMs up to Oct 2023 used Common Crawl. That shows partial overlap, but it falls short of 'pretty much every', stops before the 2024–25 models, and does not test any effect on views.
Rozado preprint: preliminary evidence that political lean is instilled mostly after pretraining. It cuts against the causal part, but the author calls it not conclusive.

reviews.rationale: The overlap in training data is only partly documented: 64% use Common Crawl, the review ends in 2023, and recent frontier data is undisclosed. The causal link is untested. The only relevant study leans against it and is itself preliminary. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is clearly met.
